title: 420 Talents of Gold, and No Address
author: QUILL
notes: Talent weight ~26-34 kg gives ~11-14 t. Great Zimbabwe link is a colonial-era myth. Not-proven line in beat 5.

beats.text: 420 talents of gold, and no address.
Solomon's fleet fetched it from Ophir. One famous guess is a myth.
beats.say: Solomon's fleet fetched it from OH-fur. One famous guess is a myth.

beats.text: The fleet sails from Ezion-geber on the Red Sea, crewed by Hiram's sailors from Tyre.
beats.say: The fleet sails from EZ-ee-on GEH-ber on the Red Sea, crewed by HIGH-ram's sailors from Tire.

beats.text: 420 talents is roughly eleven to fourteen tonnes, depending on the standard.
beats.label: 11-14 TONNES?

beats.text: Not proven: where Ophir was. The Bible never says.
beats.say: Not proven: where OH-fur was. The Bible never says.

beats.text: Guess one: southern Arabia, around Yemen.
Guess two: India's western coast, a far longer voyage.
Guess three: East Africa, far down the coast.
In 1871, explorer Karl Mauch linked Great Zimbabwe to Ophir.
beats.say: In eighteen seventy-one, explorer Karl MOWKH linked Great Zim-BAB-way to OH-fur.
beats.label: GREAT ZIMBABWE

beats.text: But Shona-speaking peoples built it, 2,000 years after Solomon. A colonial-era myth.
beats.say: But SHOH-na-speaking peoples built it, two thousand years after Solomon. A colonial-era myth.

beats.text: Arabia, India, East Africa: three real guesses, one myth.
420 talents, no address. Arabia or India: where did it come from?

youtube.description:
Solomon's ships brought 420 talents from Ophir, and the Bible never says where it was. Arabia, India or East Africa?
The location of Ophir is not proven; the Great Zimbabwe link is a colonial-era myth.
#Ophir #KingSolomon #BibleHistory #MythUnearthed
